title: Simulating the Haldane model in ultra-clean GaAs heterostructures
authors: Francesco Cioni, Lorenzo Cavicchi, Fabio Taddei, Marco Polini
abstract: The Haldane model represents the minimal lattice-based realization of a Chern insulator, exhibiting a quantized Hall conductance in the absence of Landau levels. Despite its conceptual elegance, the implementation in crystalline solids of the requisite pattern of Peierls phases breaking time-reversal symmetry remains experimentally demanding. In this work, we theoretically investigate the possibility to simulate the Haldane model in ultra-clean GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures. Our proposal relies on recent experiments in which a high-mobility two-dimensional electron gas is subject to a gate-defined honeycomb electrostatic potential and a laterally periodic magnetic field generated by patterned ferromagnetic structures. The combined electrostatic and magnetic superlattices furnish a viable route to emulate the topological properties of the Haldane model.
summary: The paper proposes an experimental route to realize the Haldane model—a key Chern insulator—by combining patterned electrostatic potentials with periodically modulated magnetic fields in GaAs heterostructures. Using advanced theoretical techniques like plane-wave diagonalization, the authors demonstrate that this combination successfully engineers non-trivial band topology, controllable via geometric misalignment parameters.
main_problem: The work theoretically investigates simulating the Haldane model, a minimal Chern insulator realization, using solid-state systems to engineer topological band structures.
main_result: Superimposing engineered electrostatic lattices with spatially periodic magnetic fields can induce non-trivial band topology, successfully mapping the low-energy physics onto the Haldane model Hamiltonian.
method: The study employs plane-wave diagonalization techniques and utilizes advanced mathematical tools like the Fukui-Hatsugai-Suzuki algorithm to calculate topological invariants (Chern number).
model_or_system: The system is modeled as spinless, non-interacting electrons in a 2D honeycomb lattice realized in ultra-clean GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures. The Hamiltonian incorporates kinetic energy, crystal potential, and coupling to engineered vector potentials derived from patterned magnetic fields.
key_observables: Chern number (C), band dispersion ($\epsilon_k$), effective mass terms ($m_H, m_S$).
important_parameters: Relative shift $\mathbf{r}_0$ between the potential and field patterns; magnetic flux amplitude ($ eta\Phi_0/2\pi$); lattice constant $a_0$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on projecting the full Hamiltonian onto a low-energy three-plane-wave manifold around the K and K' valleys, neglecting higher-shell harmonics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spatial profiles of potentials/fields for different shifts ($\mathbf{r}_0$), energy band structures along high-symmetry paths showing gap opening, and topological phase diagrams mapping Chern number $C$ vs. control parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the general Hamiltonian in a solid-state context to analyzing symmetries (P, T) and then deriving the low-energy effective Dirac Hamiltonian by treating magnetic perturbations perturbatively up to $O(A^2)$.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, materials-based blueprint for realizing topological quantum matter using external electric and magnetic field engineering, which is highly relevant for solid-state quantum simulation.
